solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Partner's pain — it could be dissipated with product from Boots?

indicators.note: dissipated means scattered, so the letters of these words are dispersed and reassembled

explanation.surface: A shopper hopes something bought at the chemist will ease a partner's sweaty discomfort.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters of PARTNERS PAIN IT are rearranged. Boots is a big British chain of chemists, so its products include toiletries; the question mark flags this as one example.
explanation.definitionFit: Deodorants and antiperspirants are toiletries sold at a high-street pharmacy such as Boots.

clue.text: Venture of son taking time and torn apart almost

parts.note: S is the standard abbreviation for son in family trees
T is the physics abbreviation for time

indicators.note: almost means the word stops one letter short of its end

parts.note: riven means split or torn apart

explanation.surface: A family venture seems doomed as the son takes his time and everything nearly falls apart.
explanation.definitionFit: To venture or make an attempt is to try hard, an effort that the answer names as a verb.

clue.text: Like imported product for sale — ought to be in wine collection

indicators.note: the instruction says the word ought should be placed inside the collection that follows

parts.note: a bin is a rack or store where bottles of wine are kept

explanation.surface: A merchant argues that imported goods ought to be part of a wine collection.
explanation.definitionFit: Goods purchased from an outside supplier and resold, rather than made in-house, are described with this phrase.

clue.text: Awkward characteristic of mum and boy in stores wandering around

parts.note: ma is an informal word for mum
a lad is a boy

indicators.note: wandering suggests these letters roam about into a new order

explanation.surface: A clumsy mother and son keep wandering around the shops.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stores' reads as shops in the surface, but 'in stores' is simply the letters to be rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Clumsiness or lack of skill is the quality of being awkward, a noun for an ungainly trait.

clue.text: Open up a foreign mammal

parts.note: un is French for a, the indefinite article
a seal is a marine mammal

explanation.surface: An instruction to cut open an exotic animal, perhaps for a dissection.
explanation.definitionFit: To break a closure so something can be opened is to undo its fastening or wax seal.

clue.text: Trance I'd suffered with bleeding heart maybe

indicators.note: suffered suggests the letters have been put through an ordeal and come out jumbled

explanation.surface: Someone recalls a trance they went through, in which they bled from the heart.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bleeding heart' sounds like an injury or a sentimental person, but it is a garden plant.
explanation.definitionFit: The bleeding heart is a common garden plant whose botanical genus has this name; 'maybe' marks it as one species.

clue.text: Name attached to Laotian possibly?

indicators.note: possibly says the letters could be arranged in another way

explanation.surface: A query about what word you would attach to someone from Laos.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both wordplay and definition: a person from Laos is a Laotian national.
explanation.definitionFit: A citizen of a country is called one of its nationals, the label attached to someone such as a Laotian.

clue.text: Reconstituted unit is occupying original position

indicators.note: something reconstituted is made up again in a fresh form, so these letters are rebuilt

explanation.surface: A military unit, newly re-formed, takes up its old post again.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin phrase means in its natural or original place, as with an artefact not moved.

clue.text: It could suggest gum that you can eat

definitions.text: It could suggest gum that you can eat

parts.words: It could suggest gum that you can eat
parts.note: the word gum, inverted on the page, mimics another short word for a cake-like treat; the answer describes such an inverted dessert

explanation.walkthrough: Turn the letters g-u-m on their heads and they roughly resemble 'wnb', a playful hint at a cake turned over; the dessert is baked with fruit at the bottom and then flipped.
explanation.definitionFit: A dessert baked with fruit underneath and then inverted for serving, so it is a cake eaten flipped over.

clue.text: Lacking any thing symbolic is dull

definitions.meaning: first meaning, read literally: without a single character, i.e. a symbol or letter
second meaning: without distinctive qualities, bland

explanation.walkthrough: A character is a written symbol, so the word split as CHARACTER-LESS literally means having no symbols.
explanation.definitionFit: Something lacking personality or distinctive features is bland, uninteresting and flat.

clue.text: Daughter avoids cutting up part of the cake

indicators.note: avoids means the daughter's letter is kept out of the word

parts.note: dicing is cutting food into small cubes

explanation.surface: A daughter keeps away while the cake is being sliced up.
explanation.definitionFit: The sugary coating spread on top of a cake is one of its layers or components.

clue.text: A church is restricting always for go- getters

indicators.note: restricting means hemming in, so the word is holds the following word inside it

parts.note: ever means always, as in for ever

explanation.surface: A church is said to be curbing ambitious people forever.
explanation.definitionFit: Ambitious, driven people who succeed in reaching their goals are achievers.

clue.text: English reader for one from Hanover?

parts.note: a lector is a reader, e.g. of lessons in church or at a university

explanation.surface: An English lecturer reading a text, perhaps for a visitor from Germany.
explanation.walkthrough: The rulers of Hanover were Electors of the Holy Roman Empire before Hanover became a kingdom; the question mark marks the example.
explanation.definitionFit: Hanover's princes held the title of prince-elector, one of those who chose the Holy Roman Emperor.

clue.text: What members of family are told

explanation.walkthrough: The clue reads as one phrase about families being told something; it splits after 'are'.
explanation.definitionFit: Relatives are connected by blood or kinship, and a story recounted to someone has been narrated.

clue.text: Deputy's circular letter

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the person next below the leader
second meaning, read cryptically: the round letter O is the second letter in the word command

explanation.walkthrough: 'Circular letter' looks like a mailshot, but it is the letter O, which sits second in the word COMMAND.
explanation.definitionFit: A deputy is the officer next in rank under the chief, who takes over in their absence.

clue.text: Old tax fund that stinks!

definitions.note: the definition is a description, standing for a thing that stinks

parts.note: cess is an old word for a tax or levy
a pool is a common fund of money

explanation.surface: An exclamation of disgust at some old tax fund that seems corrupt.
explanation.definitionFit: A pit for sewage or waste smells foul, and figuratively a corrupt place is one too.

clue.text: Cheese may give me unrest

indicators.note: may give hints that these letters could yield a different word when rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone worries that eating cheese will disturb their sleep.
explanation.definitionFit: A soft, washed-rind cow's-milk cheese from Alsace, also spelt Munster, is the answer.

clue.text: Hormone flowing repeatedly in endless lust

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: flowing suggests the letters move freely into a new order
endless means the last letter is dropped

parts.note: taken as written before its tail is dropped
repeatedly means the word in appears a second time

explanation.surface: A hormone surges again and again during unending desire.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Repeatedly in' tells you the word in appears twice, once at each end, with the rearranged stub of lust between.
explanation.definitionFit: The pancreas secretes this hormone, which regulates blood sugar levels.

clue.text: The French port is dull

parts.note: le is French for the
Aden is a port in Yemen

explanation.surface: A traveller finds a French-sounding harbour town boring.
explanation.definitionFit: Heavy and lifeless, like lead, so dull grey skies or dull prose can be described this way.

clue.text: How surprising when it goes up!

definitions.text: How surprising when it goes up!

parts.words: How surprising when it goes up!
parts.note: reads like a remark about prices rising, but describes a facial feature that lifts when we are astonished

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a shock at a rising price; the thing that rises is on your face and signals surprise.
explanation.definitionFit: Raising the hair above the eye is the classic facial expression of astonishment.

clue.text: Piece that is used for recruit

parts.note: a rook is a chess piece
i.e. is the abbreviation of id est, that is

explanation.surface: A chess or army piece that is set aside for a new recruit.
explanation.definitionFit: A rookie is a newcomer or novice, especially a raw new member of a team or force.

clue.text: Assessment of a chum going round Paris slightly confused

indicators.note: going round means the friend's letters wrap around the next group

parts.note: a pal is a chum, a friend

indicators.note: confused tells us the city's letters are muddled into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone sizes up a friend wandering around Paris in a bit of a daze.
explanation.definitionFit: An evaluation or judgement of worth, such as a staff review or a valuation, is an appraisal.

clue.text: Saint with nothing, one more or less a philosopher

parts.note: O is nothing, zero
I is the Roman numeral one
C stands for circa, Latin for about, i.e. more or less

explanation.surface: A saint with no possessions is more or less a philosopher.
explanation.walkthrough: C (circa) appears before dates meaning approximately, hence more or less.
explanation.definitionFit: A member of the ancient Greek school founded by Zeno, which taught enduring hardship without complaint.

clue.text: Tool getting line into phone

indicators.note: into says the line goes inside the phone

parts.note: TEL is the abbreviation for telephone
a row is a line

explanation.surface: A tool getting tangled into a phone cable.
explanation.definitionFit: A small hand implement used for gardening or for spreading mortar or plaster.

clue.text: 'Star plant' is king

parts.note: the aster is a daisy-like flowering plant
K is the chess abbreviation for king

explanation.surface: A claim that the star plant in the garden is the king of flowers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Star plant' looks like one phrase, since aster comes from the Greek for star; the definition is the first word alone.
explanation.definitionFit: The printed symbol * is shaped like a little star and its name derives from the Greek for small star.
